justification: Carrying span: “Since 2011 the operator has earned a quality payment in any quarter when at least ninety-two per cent of its sailings berth within ten minutes of the booked minute, and has taken it in twenty-three of the last twenty-four quarters” — twenty-four quarters is six years, taken in twenty-three, so unpaid in exactly one. A killed: the trigger is the share of sailings inside a ten-minute window, not how far behind the booked minute the average sailing berths. B killed: the clause dates from 2011 (“Since 2011”; Bexwarden “drafted the punctuality clause … in 2011”) whereas the relief boat went “in 2016”. D killed: cancelled sailings are not counted at all rather than reducing the payment — “A sailing that does not run is not late; it leaves the count altogether”, and the quarter that “lost forty-one sailings” posted “ninety-seven per cent, the highest it had ever been”.

Carrying span: “He starts with 2005. The median crossing that year took twenty-four minutes against an eighteen-minute booking. In his reading the old seventy-one per cent measured a promise nobody could keep, and five of the nine added minutes only brought the book level with the boat” — the 2005 book allowed eighteen minutes for a crossing the boat was taking twenty-four to make. B killed: “Two boats and the old book gave you a departure every twenty-five minutes”; the seventy-minute interval is the one-boat present (“One boat gives you one every seventy”), not 2005. C killed: no span on a loading allowance in 2005; the only loading-time item is the linkspan sequence introduced after the 2013 rebuild (“takes a manufacturer’s ninety seconds at each berth”), i.e. longer now, not then. D killed: lateness was measured in 2005 — “The published reliability figure stood at seventy-one per cent in 2005”, the very figure Cottam cites.

Inference from Cottam’s “Two boats and the old book gave you a departure every twenty-five minutes … One boat gives you one every seventy. Pad the book by nothing at all and you’d still have that” set against the writer’s correction “The book went from eighteen minutes to twenty-four in 2013, three years before the certificate ran out, and the interval between departures went from twenty-five minutes to thirty-two. Some of the frequency was gone before the boat was.” The timetable changes moved the interval 25→32 (seven minutes, roughly a fifth of the day’s departures); the boat’s loss moved it 32→70 (thirty-eight minutes, more than half of what remained). “Some … before the boat” concedes a minority share to the padding and leaves the larger share to the boat. A killed: the first minutes went on the book in 2013, “three years before the certificate ran out” — the withdrawal came later, not earlier. B killed: the only reason given is “the relief boat’s passenger certificate ran out and the company did not replace her”; no span links her loss to a padded book leaving her idle. C killed head-on by “Some of the frequency was gone before the boat was” — the gap had already stretched from twenty-five to thirty-two in 2013, so the withdrawal cannot be what first began stretching it.

Carrying spans: “Nobody disputes the stamps. Cottam has accepted the barrier series in writing, and does not contest the fifteen minutes. Where Cattermay’s case thins is the join. … The timetable is the reading she prefers; the stamps would bear either of the other two just as well.” The numbers are the one undisputed fact; the cause she prefers (padding) is held to be no better supported by her own data than the linkspan or the lost boat. A killed: “Nobody disputes the stamps” — her minutes are not said to show little; they are accepted as real. C killed: “the stamps would bear either of the other two just as well” — she has not shown the timetable at fault at all, not merely failed to quantify it. D killed on both halves: he does not doubt her numbers (“Nobody disputes the stamps”), and he does not grant the timetable as the probable cause — the three readings are left level.

Paragraph 1 sets the paradox: reliability “stood at seventy-one per cent in 2005. Last year it was ninety-six” while the printed crossing went from eighteen to twenty-seven minutes and “By the only measure the contract knows, the crossing has never run better”; paragraphs 2–4 give Cattermay’s (padding), Cottam’s (linkspan and lost boat) and Bexwarden’s (clause measures what people asked for) rival accounts of what links the slower journey to the rising figure; paragraph 5 weighs the accounts against each other. A killed: ramp and lost boat are only Cottam’s two causes, and the quarrel is over what caused the fifteen minutes, not which change passengers notice. B killed: confined to the Bexwarden paragraph — the consultation and the cancelled-sailings line are one strand, and the text says “None of the three is arguing about the sentence Bexwarden raised herself”. C killed: confined to Cattermay’s paragraph, and even she does not claim padding put the minutes there (“Ask me how many of them the timetable put there and I’ll give you a range, not a number”).

Gap: “the pitch does a ___ trade from eleven until the light goes” following “three hundred and forty of them go out on the east beach at a pound and ten pence a day”. “Does a brisk trade” is the fixed collocation for lively, high-volume business, which is exactly what the all-day count of hires describes. A hasty killed: connotes rushed and careless action, not volume of business; nothing in the sentence wants carelessness. B rapid and C swift killed: both describe speed of motion or of a single process and do not collocate with “trade” in the sense of business done — “a rapid/swift trade” would suggest one quick exchange, not a day-long run of hires.

Gap: “three hundred and thirty-six chairs that had ___ there since breakfast” — past perfect of the intransitive verb lie (be in a resting position) is “had lain”; the chairs are the resting subject. A lie killed: bare infinitive after “had”, ungrammatical. C laid killed: past participle of transitive lay, which requires an object (“had laid the chairs”); here nothing is being placed, the chairs themselves rest. D lay killed: lay is the simple past of lie, not a participle, so “had lay” is ungrammatical.

The paragraph before the gap frames a contrast: “What the pitch charges for and what it does are not the same thing.” Sentence one states the nominal side — “The hire is the whole of the transaction, and it has risen by ten pence in a decade”; the gap sentence states the de facto side — “the pitch is the one staffed thing on the mile between the pier and the sailing club, and Carol Gregson the one person on it who is stationary and paid” — so the connective must mark the turn from formal transaction to actual function: “In practice”. A In principle killed: reverses the logic — the hire is what holds in principle; the staffed-thing role is what holds in fact. B In addition killed: treats the two sentences as a list of like facts and loses the charges-for/does opposition the paragraph is built on. D In short killed: signals a summary, but the gap sentence introduces new material (the mile, Gregson, nine seasons) rather than compressing sentence one.

Gap: “Pressed on whether she minds the questions, she ___ that in August they are an interruption and by late September most of the job, a description rather than a complaint.” Under pressure she grants the point in part (yes, in August they interrupt) — “concedes”. C volunteers killed: to volunteer is to offer unprompted, directly contradicted by “Pressed on”. B boasts killed: nothing in the content is a boast; the tail calls it “a description”. D confesses killed: colours the reply as an admission of something personal or discreditable, which “a description rather than a complaint” expressly denies; concedes carries the pressed-into-granting sense without the guilt. Weighed A vs D seriously: both are compatible with “Pressed”, but the appositive tail rules out the confessional register and leaves concedes alone.

Gap: “It was well signed and it was free, but it was ___ used, and it shut after its second summer.” The concessive “but” and the closure demand a word meaning hardly at all: “barely used”. A widely killed: contradicts “but” and the shutting. C strongly killed: not a frequency collocate of “used”, and would likewise contradict the closure. B scantily killed: collocates with clad, dressed, furnished — not with “used”; unidiomatic even though its sense (sparsely) points the right way, and the passage’s own register elsewhere is plain idiom.

Carrying span: “Tow it, and every mesh pulls long and thin. The hole you measured with your hand is a slot by then. A haddock is round, and it has to get its width through” — which explains why going “up two mesh sizes” failed: “They did not. A whole spring on, the boxes at the harbour looked much as they had the year before.” A killed: judged over “A whole spring”, not a single trip. B killed: “The plaice were much as before, a flat fish and a stretched mesh being much the same shape” — no change for plaice is reported, and the option’s reasoning inverts the text (flat fish match the stretched slot; nothing is said about squares being the wrong shape for them). C killed: “The second change was to the hanging, not the size” — the hanging came second; the first change was mesh size.

Carrying span: “The second entries were not continuations: each named a different trade, each ran its seven years from the day of sealing, and each fell three to six years after the first.” A fresh seven-year term sealed three to six years into a seven-year first term runs three to six years past the day the first would have ended, so the boys were bound for years beyond that day. B killed: “Each of the first masters went on enrolling boys of his own for years afterwards” — the masters did not give up their trades. C killed: “Of the five fathers, two lived in the town, one farmed nine miles off, one combed wool in the next county, and one the clerk left unplaced” — only two families were in the town. D killed: “In three of the five the second premium was the larger sum”, and Ward himself went from “eleven pounds” to “fourteen pounds”.

Bärande span: “Regeln var lätt att formulera: rännan skulle luta mindre än marken nedanför den”, bekräftat av exemplet “huvudrännan faller drygt en halv meter på fyrahundra, medan myrytan under den faller ungefär det dubbla”. A fälls: det som lades “tvärs över bäcken ovanför myren” var “Ett dämme av torv, ris och sten”, inte rännan; tilloppsdiket grävdes från dämmet ut mot myrens övre kant. B fälls: “Avvägningen gjordes med vattenpass och käppar, på de mindre anläggningarna efter ögonmått”. D fälls: regeln finns just för att vattnet inte skulle “följa den till den lägsta punkten och skära sig ner där” utan lämna rännan längs hela dess längd — D är motsatsen.

Bärande span: “Det avgörande var syret. Rinnande vatten tillför hela tiden syre till det översta markskiktet, nedbrytningen av torven går fortare, och den näring som frigörs ur myren själv blir tillgänglig för växterna.” A fälls: “Bäckvatten från myrmark är brunt och slamfattigt. Någon nämnvärd mängd mineraljord avlagrades inte på ängarna vid Skrömtbäcken”; slammet vägde tyngre bara “längs de grumligare åarna i söder”. C fälls: kastar om orsakskedjan — vattnet tillför syre, det är inte nedbrytningen som förbrukar syret och därigenom frigör näring; stående vatten “stänger ute luften, nedbrytningen avstannar”. D fälls: “halten av löst näring i vattnet var för låg för att ensam förklara skördeökningen”.

Överenskommelsen införs under rubrikmeningen “Till detta kom samordningen. Fyra gårdar delade på bäcken, och den som satt överst avgjorde med sitt dämme när de nedanför fick vatten. En överenskommelse från 1858 … fördelade vattnet i turer om fyra dygn och angav i vilken ordning turerna skulle tas” — den exemplifierar tvånget att dela vattnet i bestämd ordning, förstärkt av stämningen 1870 “för att ha hållit vattnet kvar för länge”. A fälls: “Den höll i tolv år” gäller överenskommelsen, inte silängarnas brukstid, som behandlas separat (“När och varför bruket upphörde är omtvistat”). B fälls: överenskommelsen fördelar vatten, inte hö; inget span om höfördelning. C fälls: dagsverkena står i en egen mening (“omkring niohundra dagsverken fördelade på tre somrar”) under “Arbetet var det som kostade” och knyts inte till 1858.

Replikväxlingen består av två invändningar mot motpartens källor: “Pärlhage invänder att kartorna sällan går att tidfästa närmare än ett par decennier. Nolvide invänder att hennes socknar är valda bland dem som har bevarade dikningshandlingar”, och författarens slutord säger att materialet inte förmår skilja förloppen: “De två förloppen infaller i de flesta socknar inom samma tjugoårsperiod, och ingen förde bok över hur många dagar som gick åt till rännorna” — striden står alltså om vilket källmaterial som räcker. B fälls: “När och varför bruket upphörde är omtvistat”; teserna gäller varför (“fodret upphörde att vara knappt” mot “arbetskraften, som drogs till sågverken och till Amerika”), tidpunkterna är bevisningen. C fälls: de läser olika material — hon “har jämfört tidpunkterna i ett fyrtiotal socknar” med dikningshandlingar, han “har karterat rännsystemen i fyra socknar” med äldre kartor — inte samma kartor och handlingar. D fälls: Nolvides invändning gäller urvalet (“valda bland dem som har bevarade dikningshandlingar”), inte antalet; antalsskillnaden anförs aldrig som oenighetens grund.

Bärande span: “Bidraget till enskilda vägar var två kronor per meter och år … oavsett hur många som bodde vid vägen. Kvillnäsvägen är 5,4 kilometer lång … Ulvbråtsvägen … är 1,8 kilometer” → 5 400 × 2 = 10 800 kr mot 1 800 × 2 = 3 600 kr, exakt tre gånger (“Räkna gärna själv”). A fälls: “oavsett hur många som bodde vid vägen”. B fälls: per hushåll fick Kvillnäs 10 800/4 = 2 700 kr och Ulvbråt 3 600/24 = 150 kr — omvänt förhållande, vilket är författarens egen poäng: “Ett bidrag som mäts i meter och inte i hushåll gynnar den som bor glest, och det är vi som bor glest”. D fälls: “Den plogningen har för övrigt aldrig legat i bidraget utan i kommunens avtal med entreprenören”.

Bärande span: “Kommunen har alltså haft rätt i sak”, “Jag har inget att invända mot besparingen”, “Bidraget var orättvist, och jag begär det inte tillbaka” samt kravet “Det jag begär är 1,9 kilometer. Låt plogbilen gå ända fram till vändplanen och lägg sträckan i driftbudgeten”. A fälls: “svek mot landsbygden” är Sarvheds linje, om vilken författaren säger “jag tycker inte att den är riktig”. C fälls: “jag begär det inte tillbaka – inte heller ett nytt räknat per hushåll”. D fälls: han argumenterar mot en ny vändplan vid bron (180 000 kr, “drygt tio vintrars plogning”, marken inte inlöst) och vill att plogbilen fortsätter till den befintliga vändplanen vid Kvillnäs; han begär inget uppskov i väntan på bygge.

Bärande span: “Nio plåtar har moln, och även på de korten ligger samma jämna blå himmel över taken.” A fälls: den blå himlen lades också över de nio plåtarnas moln, inte bara där plåten var tom vit yta. C fälls: det är nio plåtar som har moln; korten fick “samma jämna blå himmel”, inga moln. D fälls: “Himlen ändras på varje kort” — inget kort behöll plåtens vita.

Bärande span: “Vidbring tryckte nya upplagor från samma plåt så länge ett motiv gick att sälja, och samma anvisning följde med varje gång” — vilket förklarar ingångsexemplet: ett kort poststämplat “augusti 1919” visar ett magasin som “revs hösten 1911”. A fälls: inget span om inköpta bilder; “Fotograferingen skedde med glasplåt” i firmans egen regi och plåtarna är firmans. B fälls: inget span om andra förlag som tog över motiv. C fälls: textens mekanism är nytryck från samma plåt, inte kort som låg kvar osålda i affärerna; “En del hör till lagret” förklaras omedelbart med upplagemeningen, och butikslager nämns aldrig.

Carrying span: "has taken it in twenty-three of the last twenty-four quarters" — twenty-four quarters is six years, and one quarter missed means it went unpaid once. A killed: the payment turns on a threshold share within a tolerance, "at least ninety-two per cent of its sailings berth within ten minutes of the booked minute", not on how far behind the average sailing berths. B killed: the clause dates from "Since 2011" (Bexwarden "drafted the punctuality clause for the transport authority in 2011"), whereas the second boat went only "in 2016 [when] the relief boat's passenger certificate ran out". D killed: cancelled sailings are not penalised at all — "A sailing that does not run is not late; it leaves the count altogether", and the quarter that "lost forty-one sailings" produced "ninety-seven per cent, the highest it had ever been"; nothing in the text reduces the payment for cancellations.

Carrying span: "He starts with 2005. The median crossing that year took twenty-four minutes against an eighteen-minute booking", reinforced by "five of the nine added minutes only brought the book level with the boat" — the 2005 book allowed 18 minutes while the boat took 24. B killed: "Two boats and the old book gave you a departure every twenty-five minutes"; seventy is the present one-boat figure ("One boat gives you one every seventy"). C killed: no loading claim exists; the only berth-time item is the linkspan locking sequence from the 2013 rebuild ("takes a manufacturer's ninety seconds at each berth"), i.e. berth work got longer later, the reverse of C. D killed: lateness was measured in 2005 — "The published reliability figure stood at seventy-one per cent in 2005" — and Cottam himself argues from it ("the old seventy-one per cent measured a promise nobody could keep").

Carrying spans: the interval chain 25 -> 32 -> 70. "Two boats and the old book gave you a departure every twenty-five minutes ... One boat gives you one every seventy. Pad the book by nothing at all and you'd still have that", and in the last paragraph the 2013 book change took "the interval between departures ... from twenty-five minutes to thirty-two". The timetable therefore stretched the gap by seven minutes; losing the boat stretched it from 32 to 70, more than doubling it, so it removed far more departures from the day — Cottam: "the something else is nearly the whole of it". A killed: "The book went from eighteen minutes to twenty-four in 2013, three years before the certificate ran out" — the padding came first. C killed: "Some of the frequency was gone before the boat was" — the gap first stretched in 2013, not with the boat. B killed: the text gives no reason for non-replacement ("the company did not replace her") and the 25-vs-70 contrast shows there was ample work for a second boat; nothing implies the padded book made her redundant.

Carrying spans: "Nobody disputes the stamps. Cottam has accepted the barrier series in writing, and does not contest the fifteen minutes" — the writer treats her numbers as settled — followed by "Where Cattermay's case thins is the join ... The timetable is the reading she prefers; the stamps would bear either of the other two just as well" — he declines to grant the cause she assigns. A killed: the minutes are never said to show little; they are "real" and undisputed by everyone including the writer. C killed: the writer says the stamps support the linkspan and lost-boat readings "just as well", so the timetable has not been shown at fault at all, not merely 'not by how much'. D killed: inverted on both counts — the numbers are undoubted and the timetable is not granted as probable cause; the writer also notes she "says herself that she cannot pull them apart".

Carrying spans: paragraph one sets the paradox — "By the only measure the contract knows, the crossing has never run better" (reliability 71 -> 96) against a crossing printed 18 -> 27 and a median barrier-to-ramp time "from thirty-nine minutes to fifty-four"; paragraphs three to five give three accounts of what links them (Cattermay's padding, Cottam's linkspan and lost boat, Bexwarden's clause) and the writer's weighing of "the join". A killed: the ramp and lost boat are Cottam's side only, and nothing asks which of them passengers notice. B killed: the clause, consultation and the cancelled-sailings line occupy paragraph four alone. C killed: the stamp series and the padding case are Cattermay's side only, and she herself will not make that case ("I'll give you a range, not a number"); the text is the quarrel, not one party's brief.

Gap: "the pitch does a ___ trade from eleven until the light goes". "does a brisk trade" is the fixed collocation for busy commerce, and the context is volume (three hundred and forty chairs out at a pound and ten pence a day). A hasty killed: hasty means hurried and careless, describes an action's manner, and does not collocate with "trade" as business volume. B rapid and C swift killed: both describe speed of motion or change ("a rapid rise", "a swift reply"); "a rapid/swift trade" is not idiomatic for a stall doing good business. D is the only option that yields the standard phrase.

Gap: "three hundred and thirty-six chairs that had ___ there since breakfast". After "had" the slot needs a past participle of the intransitive verb lie (to be in a resting position): "had lain". A lie killed: base form cannot follow "had". D lay killed: simple past of lie ("the chairs lay there"), not a participle. C laid killed: participle of the transitive verb lay (to put something down), which needs an object ("had laid the chairs"); the chairs here are the subject resting on the racks, so "laid" is ungrammatical.

Gap: "The hire is the whole of the transaction, and it has risen by ten pence in a decade. ___, the pitch is the one staffed thing on the mile between the pier and the sailing club". The preceding paragraph frames the contrast — "What the pitch charges for and what it does are not the same thing" — so the sentence pairs the nominal transaction (the hire) against the actual function (the one staffed, stationary person), which is "In practice". A In principle killed: it inverts the contrast; being the one staffed thing is the concrete fact, not the theory. B In addition killed: the relation is opposition, not accumulation; the paragraph is built on the charged-for/done mismatch. D In short killed: it would introduce a summary, but the sentence introduces new information (the mile, the sailing club, Carol Gregson).

Gap: "Pressed on whether she minds the questions, she ___ that in August they are an interruption and by late September most of the job, a description rather than a complaint". "Pressed" signals an admission drawn out under questioning, and admitting they are "an interruption" grants the questioner a point — that is "concedes". C volunteers killed by "Pressed": volunteering is unprompted, the opposite of being pressed. B boasts killed: calling questions an interruption is no boast, and the coda calls it a description. D confesses killed: it imports guilt or wrongdoing, which the coda "a description rather than a complaint" explicitly disclaims; she is granting a fact, not owning up to a fault.

Gap: "It was well signed and it was free, but it was ___ used, and it shut after its second summer". The "but" and the closure require low use: "barely used". A widely and C strongly killed: both assert heavy use, contradicting "but" and "it shut". B scantily killed: "scantily" collocates with clothing or furnishing ("scantily clad"), not with "used"; the natural adverb of degree for use is "barely" (or hardly/little). D is the only grammatical and idiomatic fit.

Carrying span: "Tow it, and every mesh pulls long and thin. The hole you measured with your hand is a slot by then. A haddock is round, and it has to get its width through" — towing narrows the mesh to a slot, so the two extra sizes did not give a round fish its width, which is why "They did not" see themselves out. A killed: he judged over a season, "A whole spring on, the boxes at the harbour looked much as they had the year before", not a single trip. B killed: "The plaice were much as before, a flat fish and a stretched mesh being much the same shape" — the plaice were unchanged by the turned meshes, not newly retained. C killed: "The second change was to the hanging, not the size" — the hanging was the second change; going up two mesh sizes was the first.

Carrying spans: "none for any term but seven years" and "each ran its seven years from the day of sealing, and each fell three to six years after the first" — a second seven-year term sealed three to six years into a seven-year first term ends ten to thirteen years after the first sealing, i.e. years beyond the day the first term would have ended (Ward: 1751 to 1758 versus 1755 to 1762). B killed: "Each of the first masters went on enrolling boys of his own for years afterwards" — the masters did not give up their trades. C killed: "Of the five fathers, two lived in the town, one farmed nine miles off, one combed wool in the next county, and one the clerk left unplaced". D killed: "In three of the five the second premium was the larger sum", and Ward's own went from eleven to fourteen pounds.

Bärande span: "Regeln var lätt att formulera: rännan skulle luta mindre än marken nedanför den", konkretiserat med "huvudrännan faller drygt en halv meter på fyrahundra, medan myrytan under den faller ungefär det dubbla". A dödas: det som lades "tvärs över bäcken ovanför myren" var dämmet av torv, ris och sten, inte rännan. B dödas: "Avvägningen gjordes med vattenpass och käppar, på de mindre anläggningarna efter ögonmått". D dödas: syftet var det motsatta — vattnet skulle lämna rännan längs hela dess längd "i stället för att följa den till den lägsta punkten och skära sig ner där".

Bärande span: "Det avgörande var syret. Rinnande vatten tillför hela tiden syre till det översta markskiktet, nedbrytningen av torven går fortare, och den näring som frigörs ur myren själv blir tillgänglig för växterna". A dödas: "Någon nämnvärd mängd mineraljord avlagrades inte på ängarna vid Skrömtbäcken"; slammet vägde tyngre bara "längs de grumligare åarna i söder". C dödas: mekanismen är omvänd — vattnet tillför syre; det är stillastående vatten som "stänger ute luften, nedbrytningen avstannar". D dödas: "halten av löst näring i vattnet var för låg för att ensam förklara skördeökningen".

Bärande span: "Till detta kom samordningen. Fyra gårdar delade på bäcken, och den som satt överst avgjorde med sitt dämme när de nedanför fick vatten. En överenskommelse från 1858 ... fördelade vattnet i turer om fyra dygn och angav i vilken ordning turerna skulle tas", följt av 1870-stämningen för att ha "hållit vattnet kvar för länge" — exemplet illustrerar tvånget att dela vattnet i bestämd turordning. A dödas: "Den höll i tolv år" gäller överenskommelsen, inte silängarnas brukstid; när bruket upphörde behandlas i sista stycket som "omtvistat". B dödas: inget sägs om hur höet fördelades, bara vattnet. C dödas: "omkring niohundra dagsverken fördelade på tre somrar" står i en egen mening om grävningen och har inget med 1858 att göra.

Bärande span: replikskiftet handlar helt om källorna — "Pärlhage invänder att kartorna sällan går att tidfästa närmare än ett par decennier. Nolvide invänder att hennes socknar är valda bland dem som har bevarade dikningshandlingar" — och författaren avslutar med att de två förloppen infaller "inom samma tjugoårsperiod, och ingen förde bok över hur många dagar som gick åt till rännorna", dvs. det befintliga källmaterialet räcker inte för att avgöra vare sig när eller varför. B dödas: "När och varför bruket upphörde är omtvistat", och båda anger var sin orsak (fodret upphörde att vara knappt respektive arbetskraften drogs till sågverken och Amerika). C dödas: de har inte läst samma material — hon har "jämfört tidpunkterna i ett fyrtiotal socknar" via dikningshandlingar, han "har karterat rännsystemen i fyra socknar" via kartor. D dödas: Nolvides invändning gäller urvalet ("valda bland dem som har bevarade dikningshandlingar"), inte antalet, och inget span härleder oenigheten ur att hon har fler socknar.

Bärande span: "två kronor per meter och år, och det betalades ut till samfälligheten oavsett hur många som bodde vid vägen"; Kvillnäsvägen 5,4 km mot Ulvbråtsvägen 1,8 km ger 10 800 kr mot 3 600 kr, exakt tre gånger så mycket ("Räkna gärna själv"). A dödas: "oavsett hur många som bodde vid vägen". B dödas: per hushåll får Kvillnäs 10 800/4 = 2 700 kr och Ulvbråt 3 600/24 = 150 kr — texten säger det själv: "gynnar den som bor glest, och det är vi som bor glest". D dödas: "Den plogningen har för övrigt aldrig legat i bidraget utan i kommunens avtal med entreprenören".

Bärande span: "Kommunen har alltså haft rätt i sak", "Jag har inget att invända mot besparingen", "Bidraget var orättvist, och jag begär det inte tillbaka" och sedan "Det jag begär är 1,9 kilometer. Låt plogbilen gå ända fram till vändplanen och lägg sträckan i driftbudgeten". A dödas: "svek mot landsbygden" är Gudrun Sarvheds linje, och författaren säger "jag tycker inte att den är riktig". C dödas: "jag begär det inte tillbaka – inte heller ett nytt räknat per hushåll". D dödas: han argumenterar mot vändplanen ("kostar alltså drygt tio vintrars plogning") och vill ha fortsatt plogning i driftbudgeten, inte ett uppskov tills en vändplan byggts.

Bärande span: "Nio plåtar har moln, och även på de korten ligger samma jämna blå himmel över taken" — himlen målades blå också där plåten hade moln. A dödas av samma span: färgen lades inte bara där plåten var tom. C dödas: molnen finns på nio plåtar, korten fick "samma jämna blå himmel", inga moln. D dödas: "Himlen ändras på varje kort"; det är plåtarna som har "en tom vit yta", inte korten.

Bärande span: "Vidbring tryckte nya upplagor från samma plåt så länge ett motiv gick att sälja, och samma anvisning följde med varje gång" — det förklarar hur ett kort med poststämpel "augusti 1919" kan visa ett magasin som "revs hösten 1911". A dödas: fotograferingen var firmans egen ("Fotograferingen skedde med glasplåt", färgen lades på i "firmans lokal vid torget"); inget om inköpta bilder från andra städer. B dödas: inget annat förlag nämns; Vidbring gav ut korten 1904–1929. C dödas: texten säger ingenting om att korten låg kvar i affärerna; dess egen förklaring är nytrycken från samma plåt.
